newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended weaker but off earlier lows, weighed by worries over the rand's recent slide, dealers said.
Institutional buying offered some support before close after profit-taking hit the market through most of the day. Gold shares ended soft on the back of a dull bullion price.

"There has been some buying at the end here on some industrial stocks. I think the market was just off too much and the guys came in and just bought the shares right at the lower level," one dealer said.
The rand ended at 4.5010/5040, a whisker lower than Monday's late price of 4.5000/5030.
The industrial index was last down 17.8 points at 8,501.4 points, the gold index was off 4.2 points to 1,777.1 points and the all-share index fell 31.0 points to 7,265.5 points.
Dealers said volumes traded were high at 837 million rand worth of shares. New listing First SA Food made a strong debut on the exchange.
"People liked the share but a little bit of profit-taking knocked it I suppose. I think it has been a really good listing day for the company," one dealer said.
The stock was last at 355 cents after touching a high of 375 cents in a volume worth over 20 million rand.
FSAH, which invests in niched food manufacturing operations, aims to use the cash raised in the flotation to pursue a number of expansion opportunites.

Dealers said the April all-commodities producer price index which came in at 8.8 percent year-on-year after March's 9.6 percent rise was shrugged off by the market as it was largely in line with expectations.
They said it reinforced hopes of an interest rate cut later this year.
"The market has been pretty much down because the rand is not looking too great and gold is not looking to spectacular," a dealer said.
Declining issues led advancers in the broader market by 221 to 174. There were 27 new highs and 17 new lows.
Dealers said underlying sentiment remained positive as in the last week when the market surged following a suprise peak in the Official May reserves.
But fears of capital flight after the easing of some forex controls on July clouded sentiment.
"There is a bit of nervousness in the market ahead of July," James Scott, an equities trader at stockbroking firm Societe Generale Frankel Pollak told Reuters.
"There is just no reason for anybody to be too bullish ahead of such a major event next month. We just don't know what's going to happen," another dealer added.
Other dealers said Tuesday's trade levels could be indicating the start of a period of consolidation in the market following its recent strength.
"It think what we saw could have been the start of some consolidation. Our market had a nice run last week so it's obviously going to come down," one dealer said.
The dealers said some volatility was expected later this week as futures players started to unwind their baskets ahead of next week's futures close-out.

Invicta Holdings added 55 cents to 565 cents while financial services and banking group RMB Holdings shed 25 cents to 13.40 rand on total volume of 3.5 million shares following some profit-taking on the stock.
Industrial heavyweight Barlows finished down 40 cents at 48.00 rand and South African Breweries unchanged at 132.00 rand.
On the gold board Vaal was down 75 cents to 270.75 rand and Goldfields down 50 cents to 111.50.
As on the cash market, South African share futures started knocked as nervousness about the weakened rand gripped the market.
Dealers said profit takers had shadowed around the industrial contracts while golds preferred to lie low amid an unimpressive bullion price.
By late afternoon, however, the industrial contracts had managed to rise from their early lows after taking a positive cue from better-than-expected April PPI figures, dealers said.
The all-share contract was last at 6,550/65 from 6,565 settlement, the gold contract at 814/28 from 820 settlement, and the industrial contract at 8,175/80 from 8,180 settlement.
-- Ellis Mnyandu, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
